verdict_text: NO. Step 2's formula requires each task vector to be added against the *unmodified* base (`out = base + λ(ft1−base) + λ(ft2−base)`), but the script computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1−base)` and then folds ft2 in as `tmp + λ(ft2−tmp)`, i.e. it applies the second task vector against the already-merged `tmp` instead of the original base. Algebraically this yields `out = base(1−λ)² + λ(1−λ)ft1 + λ·ft2`, not `base(1−2λ) + λ·ft1 + λ·ft2` — for λ=0.4 the base coefficient is 0.36 instead of the required 0.2, so the merged tensors will fail the grader's 1e-5 relative-Frobenius-error check. This is precisely the ordering hazard the spec warns about in "Why it is meaningful" and violates Required result step 2.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
